thread:
Raj: Quick heads-up — InsuraCo sent the security questionnaire and a POC ask. They want a 4-week POC to validate claims summarization + PII redaction. They explicitly require EU data residency (eu-west-1). Need input on deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) + ballpark pricing and success criteria. @Maria can you draft a technical approach?

Maria: Thanks. A few clarifying q's: 1) Will they send real PII data or de‑identified samples? 2) Target throughput (rps) and expected concurrency? 3) Any reqs for on‑prem/offline audit logs?

Raj: They'll share 1 week of real anonymized claims and a live stream of test traffic ~20 rps peak, sustained 5 rps. They said logs/audit must be exportable to their SIEM; they prefer not to run on-prem unless absolutely required.

Anna: Timeline: kickoff Tue week-of-Next, 4 weeks total. Week1: ingest & eval prompts, Week2: tune & iterate, Week3: performance run, Week4: handoff + exec review. Success criteria we should propose ASAP.

Maria: Proposed success criteria (initial):
- Functional: 95% redaction recall on PII spans, 95% summary relevance (human eval sample)
- Perf: p95 latency <= 250ms for generation at target tokens, 99% availability during test window
- Ops: streaming + function calls work, logs delivered to customer SIEM within 15m
- Cost: target <= $120 per 100k generated tokens (negotiable)

Tom: Deployment notes:
- Hosted (eu-west-1): fastest to start; we can isolate their org, enable prefix/KV cache per-workspace, and lock region. No infra setup on customer's side.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool in eu-west-1, predictable throughput and stronger tenancy isolation, requires a month lead for capacity & a committed spend (~$30–40k/mo estimate for 8xA10g class equivalent, rough).
- Private: VPC/On‑prem: possible but heavy — network & KMS integration, likely adds 3–6 weeks and FTE ops support.

Luis: SRE constraints: for 20 rps peaks we can run hosted with autoscaling; but sustained model context length and batchability affect latency. If they need strict p95 < 150ms and sustained traffic, recommend Dedicated. Also, we can set route-based fallbacks: start hosted, auto-failover to dedicated variants if capacity breach.

SecBot: Security questionnaire link attached: https://redwood-secure/ques/INS-2026-042 — they've flagged: encryption at rest (KMS), private key control, data residency, and SOC2 audit copies. We need to answer 3rd party access & retention.

Raj: Pricing Q from customer: are there short POC credits or a reduced dedicated intro rate? They asked for an 'evaluation price' for 4 weeks.

Maria: Proposal for POC offer:
- Option A (Fast): Hosted in eu-west-1, isolated workspace, enable audit log export, 4 weeks for $0 (credits) up to 500k tokens; overage billed at standard hosted rates.
- Option B (Predictable): Temporary Dedicated (monthly reserved) with pro‑rata intro rate — ~ $15k for the 4-week POC (covers reserved infra + priority support).
- Option C (Secure): Private in customer VPC — estimated onboarding cost + support retainer; timeline 6+ weeks — not ideal for 4‑week POC.

Maria: Suggested tech path: start with Option A (hosted) restricted to eu-west-1 and gated RBAC + KMS bring-your-own-key if they insist. Run eval suite and load generator. If we hit perf or SLO blocks, convert to Option B mid-POC.

Raj: They prefer Hosted if data residency and KMS are satisfied. They want a short doc that maps questionnaire answers to the deployment choices and risks.

Anna: I'll own the SOW + success criteria doc. Maria, can you drop the eval prompts and quick runbook into the shared drive by EOD? Tom/Luis please add infra/cost caveats. SecBot — can you prefill the security checklist answers for KMS, encryption, and audit access?

Maria: Draft eval prompts (for the claims summarization & redaction tests):
```
PROMPTS = [
  "Extract PII fields: name, SSN, DOB, policy_number, address, phone from claim_text",
  "Generate a 3‑line executive summary of the claim focusing on cause, loss amount, and recommended next step",
  "Redact PII from claim_text and return redacted_text + redaction_count"
]
EVAL_SET = 200 real claims sampled (holdout)
METRICS = {"redaction_recall": "span-level recall", "summary_quality": "human-rating 1-5"}
```

Maria: Runbook (high-level):
- Day 0: Kickoff + security review
- Day 1–3: Data ingest + baseline eval
- Week1–2: Model selection, prompt tuning, initial perf tests
- Week3: Load test and failover exercises (hosted -> dedicated path)
- Week4: Final eval, cost report, handoff
Owners: Anna (PM), Maria (SE), Tom (Infra), Luis (SRE), Raj (AE)

Tom: Quick infra caveats to add to doc:
- If we change model flavor (larger context/64k) during POC, dedicated sizing changes significantly.
- KV cache warm-up affects first 10–30 minutes of perf runs — call that out in the plan.

Luis: On monitoring: we should enable token-level cost broken down by route + per-model latency histograms. I'll create a Grafana board and basic alerts (p95 latency > 300ms, error rate > 1%).

SecBot: Pre-filled answers uploaded to /security/insuraco/INS-2026-042_answered.pdf — note: KMS BYOK requires enterprise plan for Private; hosted supports envelope keys managed; dedicated supports customer-managed KMS with additional setup.

Raj: Perfect. Next steps: Anna will share SOW + success criteria draft by EOD tomorrow, Maria will populate evals/runbook, Tom/Luis prepare infra/cost appendix, SecBot attach security answers. I'll schedule a 30m customer alignment call for Tue AM.

Anna: Sounds good. Quick check — do we want to propose a failback policy in the SOW (hosted -> dedicated auto-fallback) or keep it manual? I recommend manual trigger for the POC to avoid surprises.

Maria: Manual trigger sounds safest for test control. We'll script a simulated failover but leave final switch to operations.

Raj: OK — I'll confirm manual failover with the customer on the call. :thumbsup:

Anna: Thanks everyone — filing actions now.
